reason: The frozen decision_rule triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID on two independent grounds: (1) C2 FAIL — strict monotonicity F(20)>F(15)>F(10)>F(5) fails because F(5)=F(10)=0.0, a specification design flaw where the prereg text describes monotonicity 'from n=10 to n=20' but the frozen rule includes n=5; (2) C3 FAIL — linear extrapolation from n=15→n=20 slope 0.01316/element predicts F(50)=0.9602 (>0.80) and F(82)=1.3813 (>1.0, physically impossible for a proportion). All alternative linear anchors also exceed 1.0 (n5→n20: 1.696, n10→n20: 2.262). The audit (PASS) confirms all recomputed metrics match producer exactly. However, the empirical CDF mapping adds zero information beyond the parent positive control (audit VF5): under template invariance, F(n)=proportion(margin>0)=ranking agreement exactly by construction (residual 0.00pp at all training points, identical to B4_DIAGNOSTIC_INDICATOR). The most scientifically informative observation is the 7.6x growth deceleration (88.4% of increase in n10→n15 jump, 11.6% in n15→n20 plateau, ratio 0.1317), consistent descriptively with a threshold/phase-transition, but unvalidated with only 2 plateau points. This experiment provides no information beyond what was already known from the parent chain. Five consecutive model-based approaches have now failed: this is model-misspecification due to step-function structure (0,0,0.50,0.57), not a tunable parameter issue. The Intel lane should prioritize Docker-based direct measurement or a final bounded-function fit attempt.
